messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT created for inference-prod in eu-west-1a — elevated DNS timeouts and socket resets. Paging on-call @pd-oncall. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/inference/dns-egress

alex: I’m awake and looking. pulling resolver metrics and k/v cache errors now.

nina: seeing resolver 10.0.0.2 UDP 53 timeouts across multiple inference nodes. kvcache miss rate jumped ~60% in last 6m, token latency spikes.

jamal: logs show a lot of `i/o timeout` and `dial tcp: connection reset by peer` on connection setup to downstream model kernels.

maria: customer-facing: a small subset of Hosted API customers seeing 5xxs and high tail latency — ramping. adding status page note in a sec.

alex: running quick check: netstat shows numerous SYN_RECV => SYN retransmits. suspect intermittent egress at subnet level.

alex: trying a replicate from a problematic pod:
```
# from inference node
$ curl -v https://model-host.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.5.23 (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* Failed to receive HTTP response: Connection timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Connection timed out
```

ops-bot: config-push started to fleet: set resolver fallback to cross-az (10.0.16.2) for inference-prod.

alex: pushing agent change to replace primary resolver for nodes in eu-west-1a to use local resolver + cross-az as secondary.

maria: doing a small traffic shift as preemptive mitigation — can we move 20% of traffic to eu-west-1b reserved capacity?

ryan: initiating routing policy change: canary 20% -> eu-west-1b. Runtime accepts policy, starting slow ramp.

nina: after resolver fallback push, error-rate dropped from 18% -> 6% on canary nodes. tail latency still noisy on ~2% of requests.

jamal: digging into AWS console — route table for inference-subnet-eu-west-1a shows frequent route propagation flaps to the NAT gateway, interleaved with "stale route" notifications.

alex: can confirm. CloudWatch shows NATGatewayActiveConnections spike and route table PropagateState toggling.

ops-bot: deploy succeeded — resolver fallback applied to 120 nodes.

liz: tagging here: customers with higher request volume (acct-452, acct-998) reported retriable errors; ops team opened support tickets. I posted a short status on status.redwood.ai: "Partial egress disruption in eu-west-1a affecting small percentage of requests."

pd-oncall: I'm on call and will coordinate with AWS support. opening AWS case now with logs and timestamps.

alex: handoff to @ryan for traffic steering and canary observation. I’ll stay on AWS console and keep watching route propagation events.

ryan: increasing canary to 50%. will monitor error budget and kvcache regen. if stable for 10m, push to 100%.

nina: note — we also saw increased IMDS retries briefly (metadata requests), but that looks secondary. main culprit is DNS/egress path.

jamal: I pushed a temporary iptables rule to prevent aggressive conntrack timeouts on inference nodes (raising nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established) to avoid mid-connection drops while AWS investigates.

alex: good call. adding that to runbook as a temporary mitigation.

maria: customer impact — SLO alert triggered for 7% of requests in eu-west-1a; initial estimate ~1200 failed requests over 30m.

ryan: canary at 100% -> traffic now fully on eu-west-1b routing for inference-prod; monitoring.

nina: metrics look stable on eu-west-1b. eu-west-1a error-rate down to baseline after routing cutover and resolver fallback.

pd-oncall: AWS case updated — they saw "route table convergence" events and are escalating to networking team. provided packet captures and timestamps.

ops-bot: automation note: created temporary alert suppression for eu-west-1a noise to prevent alert storms during mitigation window.

jamal: rolling rollback of conntrack tweak scheduled for after AWS confirms fix. leaving it in place for now.

alex: handoff summary for postmortem: root suspected — intermittent route table propagation to NAT causing DNS/eDNS timeouts and connection resets; mitigations — resolver fallback, runtime routing cutover to eu-west-1b, temporary conntrack tuning, increased DNS caching TTL on nodes. AWS engaged.

maria: agreed. I'll draft the customer comms and update the support tickets with mitigation steps and ETA for a full restore.

nina: next steps: create postmortem ticket, include triggers for adding cross-az resolver as default if egress metrics spike, and add automated routing fallback in runtime for single-AZ degradation.

pd-oncall: handing back to day oncall @alex for follow-up — I'll keep AWS case and escalate if they report incomplete fix. :white_check_mark: :eyes:

alex: thanks — I'll own the follow-up items and postmortem. will keep the channel updated when AWS confirms permanent remediation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT resolved (mitigated by routing cutover and resolver fallback) — monitoring. Close when postmortem ticket is created.
